known_before_this_freeze: The rule was designed after three ledgered runs on spent pilot seeds only (the 60 unmodified episodes of the m3-protocol-1, -2 and -3 pilots, 10900 to 10919, 10300 to 10319 and 10920 to 10939, each rebuilt as its run built it): 20261108T044149Z_1a94815d (goal_diagnostic, clean 98603c4), 20261108T044845Z_616d515d (goal_rule_diagnostic, clean 15f393f) and 20261108T045902Z_f0336752 (goal_envelope_analysis, clean d8b15c1, computed from the second run's records, no simulation). In-sample findings: (a) seed 10936 frame 114 showed 13 green pixels, 2.9% of the goal's projected disc (v_g = 0.029): the gripper covered the goal; and the snapshot render's own goal there was about half hidden (v_g = 0.51), which moved protocol-3's reference centroid 5.2 px from the projected centre. At least 5 of 60 snapshot renders had a partly hidden goal: 4 whose later frames show more green than the snapshot (10304, 10906, 10936, 10937), and 10302, whose goal stays partly behind the cube in every frame (v_g never above 0.831); 10936's goal is never more than 76% visible. (b) The candidate rule 'check frames with at least 90% of the snapshot's green count' does not separate: its widened tolerance, 11.02 px, is 0.34 px under the smallest 3 cm shift; a 3 cm shift could pass in 165 eligible frames; 11 of 60 final frames are ineligible. (c) 90% of the goal's projected area (v_g >= 0.9) instead of the snapshot's count does separate in eligible frames (largest normal drift 1.75 px; a shift leaves at least 11.63 px), but 13 of 60 final frames are ineligible and on average 13.7% of type-4 injection steps have no eligible frame after them. (d) For a fully visible goal the green count is the projected disc's area: over the 56 scenes other than the four whose later frames show more green than their snapshot the snapshot's fill fraction has median 1.003 and range 0.831 (10302, partly hidden throughout) to 1.031, and 0.958 to 1.031 without 10302. Fully visible goals' centroids (v_g >= 0.98, 4,321 frames) sit on average (-0.45, -0.52) px from p in (row, column), the half-pixel convention of p (pixel centres at integer coordinates, principal point 256.0). (e) The bound holds in every one of the 10,121 frames with green: the largest excess of the centroid's distance from p over rho(v_g) r_g is 0.89 px (so 0.61 px inside the goal envelope, which adds 1.5 px). (f) Every final frame has v_g >= 0.452 (10912; next 0.500, 10302); the low finals are nominal episodes (6 of 30 nominal finals below 0.70, against 1 of 30 operator finals). (g) With the 1.5 px margin and the 0.4 floor, no unmodified episode fails, and none of 3,729,600 computed 0.03 m goal-pixel shifts (every step 1 to T - 1, every direction every 1 degree, every episode) passes; at every final frame the shifted centroid lands at least 1.05 px outside the goal envelope (2.55 px beyond rho(v_g) r_g). (h) A 0.03 m shift leaves the goal envelope, for every direction, in every frame with v_g >= 0.5, in 401 of 406 frames with 0.4 <= v_g < 0.5, and in 255 of 364 with 0.3 <= v_g < 0.4. (i) A guarantee at T (the final frame's envelope under half the scene's smallest whole-pixel 0.03 m shift, so that any lasting 0.03 m move must land outside it) would need v_g >= 0.418 to 0.605 by scene (the guarantee level, goal_geometry), and would reject 2 of the 60 unmodified episodes (10912 and 10936). The 1.5 px margin and the 0.4 floor were chosen from these numbers; every count is in-sample.

ET-M3-1.statement: Generation runs only from known sim scenes, with the initial state and asset hashes saved first; a scene-consistency check rejects injected mismatches.
ET-M3-1.candidate: a candidate is (i) a candidate manifest: the snapshot manifest's task id and version, seed, asset sha256s, cube half size and colour, and goal position; (ii) frames 0 to T of one recorded episode on that scene, rendered at 512 x 512 from the human render camera, frame 0 after restore_state and frame t after control step t; and (iii), for frame eligibility only, the joint positions and cube position that restore_state of the scene's saved initial state returns, the human render camera's centre (the translation column of the snapshot manifest's cam2world_gl), and the candidate's actions a_1 to a_T, a_t being the absolute pd_joint_pos target applied at control step t. An injection alters frames and the manifest, never (iii). No generator exists yet, so physics frames stand in for generated frames.
ET-M3-1.size_checkable_frames: The sightline is the segment from the camera's centre to the cube's initial centre. The arm's skeleton at a joint vector is arm_segments in the pinned src/vishwaroop/sim/so100_kinematics.py: line segments, without the links' thickness, from the base (world position (-0.725, 0, 0), yaw pi/2) through each joint origin of the mani_skill 3.0.1 SO-100 URDF chain in order to the fixed jaw's frame, then to the fixed jaw tip, and through the moving jaw's origin to its tip. Its clearance is the shortest distance from any skeleton segment to the sightline. Frame 0 is size-checkable when the clearance at the initial joint positions is more than 0.035 m; frame t >= 1 when frame t - 1 is and the clearance at a_t (all six values) is more than 0.035 m. So the size-checkable frames are frames 0 to n - 1, n between 0 and T + 1: the frames before the arm is first commanded near the sightline. The clearance is tested at the commanded targets only, not at the rendered arm, which lags them. Because the sightline ends at the cube's centre, a clearance above 0.035 m also keeps every skeleton segment more than 0.035 m from that centre. Both are geometric proxies; the pilot checks their premise in the simulator (stops 2 and 3). No image, mask or cube-area measurement enters this rule, so a resized, removed or duplicated cube cannot change which frames are size-checkable.
ET-M3-1.episode_kind: on even seeds the nominal scripted demo (VARIANTS['nominal']); on odd seeds an operator episode, m3-synth-lateral-miss and m3-synth-close-high alternating by seed, drawn as F2's rule in evals/M3-exit-tests.json
ET-M3-1.visibility: For a frame, r is its merged red area (the red components whose centroids lie within the merge radius of the largest one's centroid, under this protocol's pilot-set merge radius) divided by the snapshot render's merged cube area, compared unrounded. A frame shows the cube when r >= 0.02; shows no cube when r = 0; and its visibility is uncertain when 0 < r < 0.02. 0.02 is about 12 pixels of a cube of about 600 at 512 x 512. It is fixed here, not set by a pilot.
ET-M3-1.goal_geometry: From the snapshot manifest only, never from a frame or the candidate manifest. With (x, y, z) = intrinsic_cv @ extrinsic_cv @ (goal_position, 1), p, the goal's projected centre, is (row y / z, column x / z), with no half-pixel correction (pixel (i, j) is the point (row i, column j)). d is the camera-to-goal distance, the norm of extrinsic_cv @ (goal_position, 1); r_g = f_x tan(asin(R / d)) px is the goal's projected radius, with f_x = intrinsic_cv[0][0] and R = 0.015625 m, the goal sphere's radius (mani_skill 3.0.1 PickCube 'so100' goal_thresh, 0.0125 x 1.25); A_g = pi r_g^2. A frame's goal visibility is v_g = its green-mask pixel count / A_g, and its green centroid is the mean (row, column) of its green-mask pixels (the green mask as protocol-1's), both unrounded. rho(f) is the largest distance, in units of the radius, from a disc's centre to the centroid of a region covering a fraction f of it, which is the circular segment of that area: rho(f) = 4 sin^3(theta / 2) / (3 (theta - sin theta)) with (theta - sin theta) / (2 pi) = f for 0 < f < 1, and rho(f) = 0 for f >= 1. A frame's goal envelope is E = rho(min(v_g, 1)) x r_g + 1.5 px; the 1.5 px covers mask edges, shading, the half-pixel convention of p and the projected goal being a slightly elongated ellipse rather than a disc off the camera's axis. For reporting only, a scene's guarantee level is the smallest v with 2 (rho(v) r_g + 1.5) < s_min, s_min being the smallest norm, over directions every 1 degree in xy, of the whole-pixel image shift of a 0.03 m goal move (as stop (10) computes it): a final frame at or above it certainly catches a lasting 0.03 m move. In-sample r_g ran from 11.5 to 13.9 px, and guarantee levels from 0.418 to 0.605.
ET-M3-1.checker: deterministic, with no learned part, every check applied to every candidate: manifest: the candidate manifest's fields equal the snapshot's; frame_shape: every frame has the render's shape; first_frame: frame 0 equals the snapshot's saved render within the first-frame tolerance; cube_size: in every size-checkable frame, r is within the pilot-set size band [a_lo, a_hi], subject to 0.36 < a_lo and a_hi < 2.56 (protocol-2's size check, unchanged); cube_presence: the final frame T shows the cube (r >= 0.02), and a final frame that shows no cube or whose visibility is uncertain fails; extra_red: in every frame, no red component outside the merge radius has at least 0.25 x the snapshot render's cube area; goal_envelope: in every frame with at least one green pixel, the green centroid's distance from p is at most that frame's goal envelope E (goal_geometry); goal_final: the final frame T has goal visibility v_g >= 0.4, and a final frame with v_g < 0.4, including one with no green pixel, fails. There is no per-frame cube presence requirement and no upper area bound outside the size-checkable frames; the goal check has no visibility cut and no pilot-set tolerance. A snapshot render with no cube fails cube_size and cube_presence; a snapshot render with no green pixel fails goal_envelope and goal_final. A candidate with no size-checkable frame (n = 0) gets no cube_size check and still gets cube_presence. For T = 15 planning-failure episodes every frame is size-checkable, so frame T meets both rules.
ET-M3-1.how_it_tells_missing_from_occluded: No single frame tells a hidden cube from a missing one: a cube held or covered by the gripper can show no pixels at all (in-sample, 40 frames in one episode). So the rule uses when a frame comes, not what it shows. (1) Before the arm is first commanded near the camera-to-cube sightline, nothing can hide the cube, so cube_size requires the whole cube at its size; a missing or uncertain cube there fails. (2) After that, the checker accepts a frame that shows no cube or is uncertain, without deciding which; a missing cube and an occluded one are treated alike there. (3) At the final frame the cube must be seen again (r >= 0.02). Uncertain visibility at T counts as not seen and fails: the checker needs positive evidence that the cube still exists at the end. The cost: a candidate whose cube is legitimately hidden at its last frame, or knocked off the table or out of view, is rejected, which the checker cannot tell from removal. 'Shows the cube' is only a red area of at least 0.02 x the reference; it does not check position or shape after the size-checkable frames.
ET-M3-1.how_the_goal_check_tells_occlusion_from_: (1) The reference is the goal's projected centre and size from the frozen manifest, not the snapshot render, whose goal can itself be partly hidden. (2) An occluder removes part of the goal's disc and nothing else, so the centroid of what stays visible lies within rho(v_g) r_g of p whatever the occluder's shape; the envelope E allows that plus 1.5 px. A moved goal carries its visible region with it. A move of s px is certainly caught in a frame when s > 2 E, since the moved goal's visible centroid then lies within E of the moved centre and so more than E from p; for the smallest whole-pixel 0.03 m shift of each in-sample scene that holds once v_g reaches the scene's guarantee level (goal_geometry), 0.418 to 0.605 in-sample. Below that, a move is caught only if the occluder does not hide the side the goal moved toward: in-sample a 0.03 m shift left the envelope in every direction in every frame with v_g >= 0.5, in 401 of 406 frames with 0.4 <= v_g < 0.5, and less often below. (3) When most of the goal is hidden the envelope widens toward r_g + 1.5 px and a moved goal cannot be told from a hidden one; such frames are still checked, but only a larger move is caught. (4) When every frame after a goal change is poorly visible: there is no eligibility cut, so every frame with any green pixel is checked against its own envelope, and goal_final requires the final frame to show at least 40% of the goal's disc. So hiding the goal at T (v_g < 0.4, or no green) fails outright, and a change that lasts to the end is judged at T. That judgement is certain only when the final frame shows enough of the goal for its scene (its guarantee level, 0.418 to 0.605 in-sample); between 0.4 and that level a lasting 0.03 m move (and, at v_g = 0.4, a move up to 2 E, 0.031 to 0.040 m depending on the scene) can pass if the part of the goal on the side it moved toward is hidden at T. Making the goal harder to see therefore cannot hide a lasting change completely, but it can, in that band, hide one that is partly seen. Closing the band, by requiring the guarantee level at T, would have rejected 2 of 60 unmodified in-sample episodes (10912 at 0.452 and 10936 at 0.559), which the credit rule cannot carry; this draft does not require it. The cost of the 0.4 floor: a candidate whose goal is legitimately more than 60% covered at its last frame is rejected, which the checker cannot tell from a removed goal. A goal change undone before T and poorly visible while it lasts is not caught (limits).
ET-M3-1.tolerance_pilot: block 10 seeds 10940 to 10959, used for nothing else, with the episode_kind alternation. The masks (red: R > 120, G < 60, B < 60; green: G > 120, R < 80, B < 80; 8-connectivity) and the rule are protocol-1's: each tolerance is the pilot's observed extreme widened by 10% (upper extremes x 1.1, lower x 0.9). The size band takes r's extremes over size-checkable frames only, subject to 0.36 < a_lo and a_hi < 2.56; the merge radius and first-frame tolerance are taken over every frame. No presence band is set, and nothing of the goal check is pilot-set: the 1.5 px margin and the 0.4 floor are fixed here. The pilot records each candidate's n, and at every frame the simulator's cube position, the sightline clearance of the simulator's actual joint positions, and the goal's v_g, the distance of the green centroid from p, and the goal envelope E. It evaluates every condition below and, if any holds, writes nothing to evals/, lists all that hold, and the owner is told before any control or injection is generated: (1) more than 2 of the 20 pilot candidates have no size-checkable frame t with 1 <= t <= T - 1; (2) in a size-checkable pilot frame the simulator's cube centre is more than 0.005 m from its initial position; (3) a size-checkable pilot frame's r is outside [0.95, 1.05]; (4) the widened size band is not inside its limits; (5) no pilot frame is size-checkable; (6) a snapshot render shows no cube or no goal; (7) a pilot candidate's final frame does not show the cube (r < 0.02); (8) the merge radius is 60 px or more, the smallest duplicate offset, so a duplicate could merge with the cube; (9) a pilot frame with at least one green pixel has its green centroid's distance from p above its goal envelope E, or a pilot candidate's final frame has v_g < 0.4, so an unmodified candidate would fail the goal check; (10) on some pilot candidate's final frame, for some direction every 1 degree in xy, the whole-pixel image shift that a type-4 goal-pixel injection applies for a 0.03 m goal move (inject.goal_pixel_shift, rounded half up), added to that frame's green centroid, leaves the centroid within that frame's goal envelope E of p, so such an injection could pass at frame T. Stop (10) reads only the 20 pilot candidates; it does not guard the injection sources or generated trajectories. A snapshot without an exposed render camera refuses the run, before any result is written. Otherwise the tolerances go to evals/M3-checker-tolerances-p4.json with protocol_version m3-protocol-4, and its sha256 is recorded in the status ledger before any control or injection is generated.
ET-M3-1.controls: 60 unmodified candidates on block 10 seeds 10320 to 10379
ET-M3-1.injections: 10 of each of six types, seed = 10460 + 10 x (t - 1) + i for type t = 1 to 6 and i = 0 to 9 (10460 to 10519), each injected into its own unmodified source candidate on that seed, as evals/M3-exit-tests.json's ET-M3-1 'injections' describes, with protocol-2's and protocol-3's changes kept: rng = random.Random(seed); the first draw is the injection step, rng.randrange(1, T) for types 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6, and for type 3 rng.choice of the size-checkable frames t with 1 <= t <= T - 1 in ascending order; a source with T < 2 gives no injection of types 1, 2, 4, 5 or 6 (not rejected); a type-3 source with no such frame is replaced by the next unused seed from 10260 upward (to 10299) whose list is not empty, skipped seeds listed, the replacement's episode kind being its kind within the single ascending sequence 10260 to 10299; if those run out, the injection is not built and counts as not rejected. Type 6 replaces frame 0 by the snapshot render of seed + 270 (10780 to 10789), a seed range no earlier protocol named. Type 4's step stays rng.randrange(1, T): no goal visibility enters any injection's construction.
ET-M3-1.threshold: 100% of the 60 injected candidates rejected, an injection counting as rejected only when its unmodified source candidate passes every check and the injected one fails at least one (an injection whose source fails, or that is not built, counts as not rejected); and at most 3 of the 60 controls (5%) falsely rejected
ET-M3-1.if_it_fails: recorded as failed. A further revision needs m3-protocol-5, the owner's decision, a new tolerance pilot on unused block 10 seeds, and fresh controls and injections on new seeds
ET-M3-1.reported: rejections by type and by the check that caught each; every source candidate's own result; false rejections with their cause; the false-rejection count with its Wilson 95% interval; how often the size check runs (protocol-2's list); for every candidate its final-frame r, its longest run of frames with r < 0.02 and where it starts, and, from the simulator, its final cube position and whether that is on the table and projects inside the image (reporting only, not part of the rule); the number of candidates whose final frame is uncertain or shows no cube; the pilot's merge radius against stop (8), and, against stops (9) and (10), its largest value of (the green centroid's distance from p minus E), its smallest final-frame v_g, and its smallest final-frame distance of a 0.03 m shifted centroid from p minus E; for every candidate its final-frame v_g and its largest value of (the centroid's distance from p minus E) (in the run record, per frame: v_g, the centroid's distance from p and E); the candidates whose final frame has 0.4 <= v_g < the scene's guarantee level (goal_geometry); for each type-4 injection its subtype, step, shift and the first frame where goal_envelope failed; each type-3 injection's seed, skipped seeds, step and T; what happens at n = 0 and when visibility is uncertain (above); the limits below; and a statement that controls are physics renders, so this does not estimate false rejection on generated frames (ET-M3-2 measures that)
ET-M3-1.risk_before_freezing: estimated, not measured. goal_envelope: no in-sample frame came within 0.6 px of failing (largest distance minus E: -0.61 px over 10,121 frames), so its false rejections need occlusion, shading or a goal position unlike the sample's. goal_final is the new binding risk, and the evidence for its rate is thin: 0 of 60 final frames below 0.4, the nearest at 0.452 and 0.500 (both nominal episodes; half the injection sources are nominal), which bounds the per-episode rate only below about 5% (95%, rule of three). Per-episode rates of 1 in 300, 1 in 100 and 1 in 60 would give 18%, 45% and 64% that at least one of the 60 sources fails goal_final (one failing source fails the test), and, with protocol-3's estimate of 17% to 31% for cube_presence, 32% to 44%, 55% to 62% and 70% to 75% that at least one source fails one or the other (taking the two failures as independent). More than 3 of 60 controls failing: under 2% for goal_final alone up to 1 in 60, and, with cube_presence, about 0.1% to 0.3%, 0.8% to 1.6% and 3.1% to 4.8% at those rates. The pilot itself stops under (9) with probability 6%, 18% and 29% at those rates. A 0.3 floor would lower goal_final's rate (the sample cannot say by how much) and widen the band of (4) in which a partly seen lasting move can pass (in-sample a 0.03 m shift was caught in 255 of 364 frames with 0.3 <= v_g < 0.4). Type 4's goal-pixel shift relies on goal_envelope (in-sample none of 3,729,600 passed); type 2 relies on extra_red (stop 8).
ET-M3-1.limits: A cube that disappears after the size-checkable frames and reappears before the end is not caught by cube_presence, and a size error after those frames is not caught by cube_size; an enlarged cube is caught only in size-checkable frames. ET-M3-1 shows that the checker catches a removal that persists to the end, a duplicate, and a resize that starts before the arm approaches. ET-M3-2 has to judge presence and size in the frames between. For the goal: a goal change that is undone before the final frame is caught only in frames where enough of the goal shows (in-sample a 0.03 m move left the goal envelope in every frame with v_g >= 0.5, and less often below); a lasting change is judged at frame T. goal_envelope checks the centroid of all green in the frame, not the goal's size or shape: extra green away from the goal is not rejected, and can pull a moved goal's centroid back onto p, so a generated frame with a moved goal and a second green region can pass (in-sample no frame showed more than 1.031 of the goal's area, so sim frames have no stray green). A lasting move is judged at T but is certain to be caught there only above the scene's guarantee level (how_the_goal_check_tells_occlusion_from_a_moved_goal (4)). ET-M3-2 has to judge temporary disappearances, late resizes, poorly visible goal changes and stray green in generated trajectories.
